message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you decide). Points are earned by collecting cards from opponents when you finish your own hand. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | | **Turn order** | Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a reverse card is played). | | **Playing a card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top card on the discard pile. | | **Special cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Uno** | When you have one card left, shout “UNO!” before your turn ends. If another player catches you not saying it, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a round** | The first player to get rid of all their cards wins the round. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of the cards left in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip, Reverse, Draw Two = 20 points.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points.
Winner’s score = sum of opponents’ points. | | **Next round** | Continue playing until someone reaches the target score (e.g., 500). | **Optional house rules** - *Stacking*: Allow players to stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing. - *No Wild Draw Four rule*: Some groups forbid playing Wild Draw Four unless you truly have no other playable card. - *Custom scoring*: Adjust the target score or add extra points for special cards. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak the rules to suit your group.
